purpose: Discovery register for potentially useful open industrial-maintenance knowledge and data. It is not an imported fault database.
policy: Do not copy repository contents or datasets into this project until the exact license, dataset terms, attribution requirements, and provenance are checked. Research papers and public GitHub visibility do not by themselves grant redistribution rights. Permissively licensed dataset metadata and candidate snapshots may be stored in isolated research folders with attribution and source evidence; no candidate data is loaded by runtime until separately reviewed and approved.

sources.contentsReviewed: Inspected the methodology and source code. Hydraulic analysis filters stable cycles, groups contiguous operating-condition blocks and uses StratifiedGroupKFold with disjoint train/test groups; it excludes virtual CE/CP and unresolved SE channels. Paderborn protocol splits by bearing ID, holds all recordings/conditions from one bearing together and documents duplicate recording groups. Raw sensor files are described as local and are not committed.

qualityNotes: Strong leakage-control reference: hydraulic grouping by condition blocks and Paderborn grouping by physical bearing.
Paderborn measuring-log Unit fields are reported empty; signal units/scaling remain unverified in the repository notes.
The repository identifies duplicate Paderborn recordings and excludes them from the first protocol.
Its hydraulic findings are descriptive predictive comparisons, not causal mechanisms or maintenance procedures.
No LICENSE file; source headers reserve all rights.
sources.dataLeakage: Hydraulic: split by contiguous condition block; Paderborn: split by bearing ID, never by recording windows. The README explicitly says condition blocks are not verified independent experimental runs.
sources.dependencies: Python, NumPy, pandas, scikit-learn and a Conda environment; research scripts and local raw data paths.
sources.android: Do not port code. Reuse the methodological lesson—asset/run/block-aware splits—only as a design principle.
